title: Routine vs New Decisions | Principles of Management Ep 22
description:
Should the boss decide everything? Chai Corner now has five outlets, and forty questions a day land on Ravi: milk is low, a customer wants a refund, a new tea shop opens near the college. In this animated lesson, Ravi learns to sort his decisions.

You will meet Herbert Simon, who named the two kinds in his 1960 book The New Science of Management Decision. Programmed decisions are routine and repetitive, so you write a rule once. Non-programmed decisions are new and unstructured, so they need judgment. We watch Ravi sort one day of questions live, see the three tools of programmed decisions (rules, procedures and policies), see why new, high-stakes choices go to the top, and find rules, procedures, policies, judgment and computers at work today in a bank, an airline, a shop and a hospital. The human side is honest too: rules are fast, cheap and fair, but they go stale and can be silly when followed blindly, and Simon saw the two types as ends of one line, not two boxes.

This is Episode 22 of our Principles of Management series for MBA, BBA and commerce students.
